summary: Audit each of the 36 religion-wedge assignments in SCRIPTURE_RELIGIONS — flag conflations, propose splits/moves/merges so each wedge is a distinct tradition with academic integrity

result.summary: Synthesized 5 goblin audits into a new SCRIPTURE_RELIGIONS taxonomy growing from 36 to 56 wedges. The major restructures: Christianity splits into proto-orthodox/Christian-Gnosticism/Esoteric-Christianity (Brakke + Hanegraaff); Judaism splits off Samaritanism + Sabbatean-Frankist (Scholem + Maciejko); the bundled gnostic-dualist wedge becomes two distinct religions Mandaeism + Manichaeism (Buckley + BeDuhn); Chinese splits into Confucianism + Daoism (Kohn + Lagerwey); Buddhism sheds Bön (Kvaerne); esoteric-occult splits into 4 historically-distinct waves (Western Alchemy, Renaissance Esotericism, Rosicrucian/Masonic, Modern Occult Revival per Hanegraaff/Yates/Stevenson); modern-syncretic + modern-religions explode into individual NRMs (Cheondogyo, Tenrikyō, Cao Đài, Scientology, LaVeyan Satanism) with Ambedkar → Buddhism and Iqbal → Islam; afro-diasporic splits into Haitian Vodou + Lucumí-Santería; mesoamerican splits into Maya + Aztec-Mexica with the duplicate umbrella retired; indigenous-na splits into Diné/Lakota/Haudenosaunee/Lenape. All seven goblin "keep-as-is" verdicts honored (Islam, Hermetic, Mystery Cults, Neoplatonism, Israelite, Canaanite, Hurro-Hittite, Egyptian, Zoroastrianism, Hinduism, Jainism, Sikhism, Shintō, Yoruba, Andean, Polynesian, Aboriginal, Bahá'í, Mormon, Druze, Yazidi). This unlocks the MASSIVE-WIN cross-wedge wires John needs: proto-orthodox ↔ Christian-Gnosticism polemics, Bön ↔ Vajrayāna mutual influence, Theosophy ↔ Anthroposophy 1912 schism, Vodou orisha ↔ Yoruba òrìṣà transmission.

final_taxonomy.label: Christianity
final_taxonomy.rationale: Proto-orthodox / Catholic / Orthodox / Protestant trunk only. Heterodox Gnostic-Christian and esoteric-Christian streams lifted out so the cosmological war (creator-God vs demiurge, Nicene Trinity vs Boehmian theosophy) becomes visible as cross-wedge wires rather than buried inside one wedge.

final_taxonomy.label: Christian Gnosticism
final_taxonomy.rationale: Suppressed Gnostic-Christian stream that proto-orthodoxy declared heresy: Sethian/Valentinian (Nag Hammadi), medieval radical-dualist successors (Cathar/Bogomil), and the heterodox apocryphal cluster (Letter to Flora is itself Valentinian per Ehrman 2003). Brakke 2010 + King 2003 + Lambert 1998 + Stoyanov 2000.

final_taxonomy.label: Esoteric Christianity
final_taxonomy.rationale: Post-Reformation visionary/esoteric-Christian transmission Boehme → Vaughan → Swedenborg → Eddy → Kybalion → ACIM that Hanegraaff 2012 treats as a coherent Western-esoteric-Christianity lineage distinct from mainline trunk.

final_taxonomy.label: Judaism
final_taxonomy.rationale: Normative rabbinic Judaism + Kabbalah trunk (Scholem 1941 places Kabbalah firmly inside Judaism). Samaritan and Sabbatean-Frankist lifted out as separate wedges since both involve definitional ruptures the parent rejected.

final_taxonomy.label: Samaritanism
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct Israelite-derived community: own Pentateuch recension, Mt. Gerizim cult, rejects Prophets/Writings/Jerusalem Temple. Pummer 2016 treats Samaritans as a religion that diverged from Second Temple Judaism, not a Jewish sect.

final_taxonomy.label: Sabbatean-Frankist messianism
final_taxonomy.rationale: Antinomian post-Jewish messianic movement: Sabbatai Zevi excommunicated by every major rabbinic court, Jacob Frank converted to Catholicism in 1759 and claimed personal divinity. Scholem 1973 + Maciejko 2011 frame this as a definitive break from normative Judaism.

final_taxonomy.label: Islam
final_taxonomy.rationale: All corpora share Quranic foundation, hadith framework, prophetic chain culminating in Muhammad — Sunni / Shia / Sufi / Ishraqi / Isfahan / Alevi all self-identify as Islamic. Iqbal added (was misfiled under modern-syncretic). Druze + Yazidi correctly already split out. Hodgson + Daftary + Corbin.

final_taxonomy.label: Hinduism
final_taxonomy.rationale: All seven sampradāyas share Vedic śruti substrate, Brahminical lineage, overlapping pantheon. Flood 1996 + Lipner 2010 treat Vaiṣṇava / Śaiva / Advaita / Śākta as textbook sub-traditions within Hinduism.

final_taxonomy.label: Buddhism
final_taxonomy.rationale: Theravāda / Mahāyāna / Vajrayāna vehicles share historical Buddha, Triple Jewel, Four Noble Truths. Ambedkar's Navayana added (he self-identified as Buddhist). Bön split off — Kvaerne 1995 + Karmay 1972 treat Yungdrung Bön as a sister tradition with its own founder Tönpa Shenrab.

final_taxonomy.label: Yungdrung Bön
final_taxonomy.rationale: Independent founder (Tönpa Shenrab Miwoche, not Śākyamuni), distinct origin culture (Zhang-Zhung), own scriptural canon (Bön Kanjur), parallel cosmology that absorbed and was absorbed-by Vajrayāna 11th c. Splitting makes the Bön ↔ Nyingma Dzogchen priority dispute visible as a cross-wedge wire.

final_taxonomy.label: Zoroastrianism
final_taxonomy.rationale: Single-canon religion: Old Avestan Gāthās → Younger Avesta → Pahlavi visionary corpus → Dēnkard already encodes the diachronic layers per Boyce/Skjærvø.

final_taxonomy.label: Jainism
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct founder (Mahāvīra / 24 Tīrthaṅkaras), distinct ontology (jīva/ajīva, anekāntavāda), distinct soteriology. Dundas 2002.

final_taxonomy.label: Sikhism
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct founder (Gurū Nānak), distinct theology (Ik Onkar, miri-piri), distinct community (Khalsa, 1699), eternal Gurū installed 1708. Cross-wedge wires to sant-nirguna + sufi-persian remain critical.

final_taxonomy.label: Bahá'í
final_taxonomy.rationale: Doctrinally distinct post-Islamic new revelation (1844 Báb, 1863 Baháʼu'lláh), own scripture (Kitāb-i-Aqdas), progressive-revelation cosmology. Smith 2008 + MacEoin 2009.

final_taxonomy.label: Mormon (LDS)
final_taxonomy.rationale: 19th c. American restorationist new revelation: own scripture (Book of Mormon, D&C, PoGP), distinct cosmology (premortal existence, eternal progression, embodied Heavenly Father) that Nicene Christianity rejects. Bushman 2005.

final_taxonomy.label: Israelite (pre-exilic)
final_taxonomy.rationale: Pre-exilic Israelite Yahwism distinct from post-exilic Judaism. Splitting enables the MASSIVE-WIN wire to Canaanite El/Asherah substrate. Smith 2002 + Dever 2005.

final_taxonomy.label: Canaanite / Ugaritic
final_taxonomy.rationale: West Semitic Ugaritic religion (Baal Cycle, ritual texts) — the parent-substrate Israelite Yahwism partially absorbed. Essential for cross-wires (YHWH inherits El's epithets; Leviathan ← Lōtan). Smith 2001 + Pardee 2002.

final_taxonomy.label: Hurro-Hittite
final_taxonomy.rationale: Anatolian Bronze Age religion with own pantheon (Tarhunna, Telipinu, Kumarbi). Kumarbi Cycle is the documented Indo-European succession-myth bridge to Hesiod's Theogony per M.L. West 1997 — only visible if Hurro-Hittite stays separate.

final_taxonomy.label: Egyptian (ancient)
final_taxonomy.rationale: Continuous ~2400 BCE → 400 CE tradition; broadly stable theological substrate (Ra/Osiris/Isis/Horus/Ma'at) across Old/Middle/New Kingdom sections. Atmana interlude correctly internal section per scholarly consensus. Assmann 2001 + Hornung 1982.

final_taxonomy.label: Greek (ancient)
final_taxonomy.rationale: Greek pantheon canonical corpus (Hesiod, Homeric Hymns, Orphic-adjacent). Mystery cults + Neoplatonism + Hermetic correctly held as separate adjacent wedges to surface the inheritance relationships as cross-wires.

final_taxonomy.label: Mesopotamian (Sumerian + Akkadian + Babylonian + Assyrian)
final_taxonomy.rationale: Sumerian + Akkadian + Babylonian + Assyrian form continuous textual canon (Enūma Eliš, Atrahasis, Gilgamesh) with successive linguistic recensions per Black & Green, Foster. Label cleaned of stale 'Canaanite' double-claim; empty canaanite-ugaritic section in SCRIPTURE_CORPORA must be removed (Lane A).

final_taxonomy.label: Mystery Cults
final_taxonomy.rationale: Eleusinian / Orphic / Dionysian / Isiac / Greco-Egyptian magical bundled per Burkert 1987 + Bowden 2010 unified-category treatment. At current 6-text depth split would create single-text wedges that obscure cross-cult resonances; defer split until Lane A backfills 3+ texts per cult.

final_taxonomy.label: Neoplatonism
final_taxonomy.rationale: Coherent late-antique school (Ammonius → Plotinus → Porphyry → Iamblichus → Proclus → Damascius) with distinct cosmology (One → Nous → Soul) and canon (Enneads + Elements of Theology). Surfaces the Plotinus → Pseudo-Dionysius → Arabic-Neoplatonism → Ficino transmission spine. Shaw 1995 + Wallis 1972.

final_taxonomy.label: Hermetic
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct Greco-Egyptian revelatory tradition with own prophet-chain (Hermes Trismegistus → Tat → Asclepius), own cosmogony (Poimandres anthropos-descent), continuous reception (Greek → Coptic NHC VI → Latin Asclepius → Renaissance Pimander). Fowden 1986 + Copenhaver 1992.

final_taxonomy.label: Norse / Finno-Ugric
final_taxonomy.rationale: Norse Eddic (Poetic + Prose Edda) plus Finno-Karelian (Kalevala) North-European mythological corpus. Kept together as the cross-cultural Northern European mythopoetic family — splitting at current corpus depth would obscure shared substrate.

final_taxonomy.label: Maya
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct pantheon (Itzamná / Kʼinich Ajaw), distinct calendar (Long Count), distinct script (logosyllabic), distinct languages. Popol Vuh + Chilam Balam + Dresden Codex. Madrid + Paris codices flagged for Lane A backfill. Tedlock 1996.

final_taxonomy.label: Aztec / Mexica
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct pantheon (Huitzilopochtli / Tezcatlipoca / Quetzalcóatl-Ehécatl), distinct calendar (xiuhpōhualli), pictographic script, Nahuatl language. Florentine Codex + Codex Borgia + Historia. Cantares Mexicanos + Codex Boturini flagged for Lane A. Carrasco 2014.

final_taxonomy.label: Shintō
final_taxonomy.rationale: Both corpora share kami substrate, imperial-genealogical theology, 8th–10th c. court codification. Kojiki/Nihon Shoki = mythistorical chronicles, Engishiki = liturgical continuation. Buddhist syncretism (honji suijaku) correctly kept out — pure-land/zen housed under buddhism per Kuroda 1981.

final_taxonomy.label: Confucianism
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct social-ritual humanism centered on lǐ / rén / xiào with Five Classics as state-orthodox canon (Han through Qing examinations). Treated as separate tradition since the Sima Tan Six Schools essay (~110 BCE). Taylor 1990 + Lagerwey & Kalinowski 2009.

final_taxonomy.label: Daoism / 道教
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct cosmological naturalism centered on Dào / wú-wéi / zìrán with own institutional religion (Tianshi / Shangqing / Lingbao / Quanzhen) and own canon (Daozang 1445 CE, 1476 texts). Splitting from Confucianism makes Daoism ↔ Chan/Zen and Daoism ↔ Chinese alchemy wires explicit. Kohn 2000.

final_taxonomy.label: Mandaeism
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct Aramaic-speaking Iraqi/Iranian gnostic-baptist community (~60,000 today) with John the Baptist as central prophet, Ginza Rba as scripture, continuous since 2nd c. CE. Buckley 2002 + BeDuhn 2000 treat as completely separate from Manichaeism despite shared 'gnostic-dualist' family resemblance. (Lane A first: split existing mandaean-manichaean corpus into mandaean-corpus + manichaean-corpus.)

final_taxonomy.label: Manichaeism
final_taxonomy.rationale: Religion founded by Mani (216–274 CE) under Sasanian patronage, propagated North Africa → Tang China, extinct by 14th c. Own canon (Cologne Mani Codex + Kephalaia + Shabuhragan). Bundling with Mandaeism was the same category-error as bundling Christianity with Islam. Lieu 1992 + BeDuhn 2000.

final_taxonomy.label: Yoruba (Ifá)
final_taxonomy.rationale: African-continental Tier-1 substrate: 256 Odù Ifá canon, babaláwo priesthood, Olódùmarè + Òrìṣà pantheon, pre-colonial continuity. Stays separate from Afro-diasporic to make transmission wires (Lucumí Eleguá ↔ Yoruba Èṣù) visible. Bascom 1969 + Peel 2000.

final_taxonomy.label: Haitian Vodou
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct Fon/Ewe/Dahomean + Kongo African substrate, French Catholic overlay, Kreyòl liturgy, own priesthood (houngan/manbo). Splitting from afro-diasporic surfaces cross-Atlantic divergence from Lucumí. McCarthy Brown 2001.

final_taxonomy.label: Lucumí / Santería
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct Yoruba African substrate, Spanish Catholic overlay, Lucumí ritual language, own priesthood (santero/santera). Adjacent placement to Yoruba makes orisha ↔ òrìṣà cognate-wires explicit. Palmié 2002 + Matory 2005.

final_taxonomy.label: Andean (Quechua)
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct civilizational tradition (Inti, Viracocha, Pachamama, huaca cult). Huarochirí Manuscript (~1608 Quechua) is the single most important indigenous-language Andean text. Backfill flagged: Guamán Poma, Pachakuti Yamqui. Salomon & Urioste 1991.

final_taxonomy.label: Polynesian
final_taxonomy.rationale: Hawaiian Kumulipo + Māori cosmogonic chants share single Austronesian/Proto-Polynesian substrate (Tāne/Kāne, Tangaroa/Kanaloa, Rongo/Lono cognate pantheon). Intra-Polynesian divergence handled at corpus-section level. Valeri 1985 + Kirch 2010.

final_taxonomy.label: Diné / Navajo
final_taxonomy.rationale: Athabaskan language family, Blessingway/Hózhǫǫjí ceremonial system, distinct from Plains or Eastern Woodland traditions. Sturtevant Handbook vol. 10 Southwest.

final_taxonomy.label: Lakota / Oglala
final_taxonomy.rationale: Siouan language family, Sacred Pipe + Seven Rites (Black Elk transmission), distinct Plains cosmology. Holds Black Elk Speaks + The Sacred Pipe. Sturtevant Handbook vol. 13 Plains.

final_taxonomy.label: Haudenosaunee
final_taxonomy.rationale: Iroquoian language family, Gayanashagowa (Great Law of Peace) as political-religious constitution, distinct Northeast Woodland tradition. Sturtevant Handbook vol. 15 Northeast.

final_taxonomy.label: Lenape (Walam Olum)
final_taxonomy.rationale: Eastern Algonquian, Walam Olum — must be Tier-1-flagged as widely-held 19th c. Rafinesque forgery (Oestreicher 1996, Goddard 2007) while preserving the document as a node in its own right. Reserved as standalone wedge pending a broader eastern-Algonquian backfill.

final_taxonomy.label: Aboriginal Australian
final_taxonomy.rationale: Recognized single religious-cultural complex spanning 250+ language groups via shared ontology (Ancestral Beings, Songlines, country-law) per Stanner / Berndt / Morphy. Lane A backfill flagged: Wawilak Sisters, Djang'kawu, Rainbow Serpent.

final_taxonomy.label: Rastafari
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct Jamaica-1930s religion: Jah Rastafari = Haile Selassie I, Kebra Nagast read against KJV + Holy Piby + Garvey, own community (nyabinghi, ital, ganja sacrament). Lane A flagged: replace stub entries with Holy Piby (Rogers 1924), Promised Key (Howell 1935), Garvey Philosophy & Opinions. Chevannes 1994.

final_taxonomy.label: Druze
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct esoteric tradition emerged Fatimid Egypt 1017–1043 CE, closed initiation 1043 CE: transmigration replaces resurrection, al-Ḥākim as seventh theophany, Neoplatonic-Pythagorean cosmic hierarchy. Decisively crossed out of Islam per Firro 1992 + Halm 2014.

final_taxonomy.label: Yazidi
final_taxonomy.rationale: Distinct West-Iranian/syncretic tradition with Melek Taus / Peacock Angel cosmology that explicitly inverts both the Iblīs and Lucifer-fall narratives. Own sacred texts (Kitêba Cilwe + Mishefa Reş + qewls). Kreyenbroek 1995 + Açıkyıldız 2010.

final_taxonomy.label: Cheondogyo (Donghak)
final_taxonomy.rationale: Tier-1 distinct Korean religion (1860): founder Choe Je-u, scripture Donggyeong Daejeon, Hanullim monotheist innovation, revolutionary lineage (Donghak Peasant Revolution 1894). Baker 2008.

final_taxonomy.label: Tenrikyō
final_taxonomy.rationale: Founding Japanese shin-shūkyō (1838): founder Nakayama Miki, scripture Ofudesaki, Oyagami / joyous-life theology. Hardacre 1986. Future grouping under a 'japanese-shin-shukyo' family band possible once Ōmoto / Sōka Gakkai corpora wire up.

final_taxonomy.label: Cao Đài
final_taxonomy.rationale: Deliberately syncretic Vietnamese Third-Alliance religion (1926) with French Spiritist roots. Distinct founder claims, own canon, own ecclesial structure. Blagov 2001.

final_taxonomy.label: Western Alchemy
final_taxonomy.rationale: 13th–18th c. operative/spiritual alchemy: Rosarium Philosophorum, Splendor Solis, Paracelsus, Sendivogius, Starkey, Ripley, Ashmole. Operates within Christian-natural-philosophy frame. Principe 2013.

final_taxonomy.label: Renaissance Esotericism
final_taxonomy.rationale: 15th–17th c. Christian-Hermetic-Kabbalistic magic: Ficino, Pico, Reuchlin, Agrippa, Dee, Fludd, Kircher, Khunrath. Hanegraaff 2012 treats this as the foundational 'rejected knowledge' stratum distinct from both medieval alchemy and 19th c. occult revival.

final_taxonomy.label: Rosicrucian / Masonic
final_taxonomy.rationale: Fraternal-initiatic literary tradition: Fama 1614, Confessio 1615, Chymical Wedding 1616, Anderson Constitutions 1723. Yates 1972 + Stevenson 1988 group as a single fraternal-utopian cluster distinct from operative alchemy and 19th c. occult orders.

final_taxonomy.label: Modern Occult Revival
final_taxonomy.rationale: 19th–20th c. 'occulture' break with churchly religion (Hanegraaff 1996, 2012; Owen 2004). Theosophy 1875, Anthroposophy 1912 (Christology split from Theosophy per Zander 2007), Wicca 1954 (Hutton 1999 independent witchcraft-revival lineage). Thelema lifted into its own wedge as a new-revelation claim.

final_taxonomy.label: Thelema
final_taxonomy.rationale: Liber AL vel Legis (1904) is received scripture per Crowley — a new-revelation claim analogous to Bahá'í Kitāb-i-Aqdas or Mormon's Book of Mormon. Explicit break with Golden Dawn / Mathers per Pasi 2014. Splitting from modern-occult-revival surfaces the Crowley-vs-Golden-Dawn-vs-Theosophy polemics as cross-wires.

final_taxonomy.label: Scientology
final_taxonomy.rationale: 20th c. American NRM: Hubbard auditing / thetan soteriology, corporate-church structure. Urban 2011.

final_taxonomy.label: LaVeyan Satanism
final_taxonomy.rationale: 20th c. American NRM: Anton LaVey atheistic carnal-self-deification + ritual theatre (Church of Satan 1966, Satanic Bible 1969). Dyrendal/Lewis/Petersen 2015.

controversial_calls: Christian Gnosticism split: pulls Nag Hammadi + Cathar/Bogomil + christian-apocrypha out of Christianity. Strong scholarly basis (Brakke, King, Lambert, Stoyanov, Ehrman) but reasonable people argue these were INTRA-Christian heresies, not separate religions. The investigative payoff is that proto-orthodox patristic-corpus is literally the anti-Gnostic polemical canon (Irenaeus, Tertullian, Hippolytus) — bundling attacker and target erases the cosmological war. Sign-off needed: is the Codex investigation served better by surfacing that war as a cross-wedge wire (split) or as an internal-Christianity tension (keep)?

Esoteric Christianity split: pulls Boehme + Swedenborg + New Thought (Eddy + Kybalion + ACIM) out of Christianity. Hanegraaff treats this as a coherent Western-esoteric-Christianity transmission line, but Boehme + Vaughan are Lutheran/Anglican mystics who never left mainline churches — splitting them is more aggressive than the Gnostic split. ACIM is genuinely heterodox. Possible middle path: keep Boehme/Vaughan under Christianity (mystical-Christian sub-section) and only split Swedenborgian-New-Church + new-thought-corpus.

Cathar/Bogomil placement: I assigned to christian-gnosticism, but the transmission chain Paulician → Bogomil → Cathar runs through Manichaean dualism per Stoyanov. Could instead live as its own wedge ('medieval-dualist') OR adjacent to Manichaeism. Christian-Gnosticism placement preserves the Christian-internal framing; Manichaean-adjacent placement preserves the dualist-transmission framing. Pick one investigative axis.

Mandaeism + Manichaeism split: requires Lane A to first split the bundled 'mandaean-manichaean' corpus in SCRIPTURE_CORPORA into mandaean-corpus + manichaean-corpus. Both are textually documented enough to do this cleanly. Goblin verdict was unanimous on the split — flagging only because it's a Lane A blocker on the religion-wedge change, not a judgment call.

Thelema as its own wedge vs holding inside modern-occult-revival: Thelema is a new-revelation claim (Liber AL vel Legis as received scripture from Aiwass 1904), structurally identical to how Bahá'í + Mormon are treated. But it shares 19th c. occult-revival genealogy with Theosophy. I split it out to match the new-revelation pattern; defensible to fold back into modern-occult-revival as a sub-section.

Lenape Walam Olum as standalone wedge: it's widely held to be a 19th c. Rafinesque forgery (Oestreicher 1996, Goddard 2007). Standalone-wedge treatment preserves it as a node but might give too much prominence to a likely fabrication. Alternative: hold under a future broader 'eastern-algonquian' wedge that includes attested Algonquian traditions, with Walam Olum flagged as Tier-1-disputed inside the corpus.

Ambedkar → Buddhism move: Ambedkar self-identified as Buddhist and Navayana is treated as a Buddhist reform movement by Engaged Buddhism scholars (Queen & King 1996). But some scholars treat Navayana as distinct enough from Theravāda / Mahāyāna / Vajrayāna to warrant a separate wedge. Holding under Buddhism as 'modern-navayana' corpus is the scholarly mainstream call but flag for John.

Iqbal → Islam move: Iqbal's Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam is an Islamic-modernist philosophy text. Clearly belongs under Islam. Only flag is whether to introduce a dedicated 'islamic-modernism' corpus alongside the existing islamism-corpus (they are NOT the same — modernism = Iqbal/Abduh/Rahman intellectual project; islamism = Maududi/Qutb political-Islam project).

Defer split until Lane A backfills 3+ texts per cult.
